source.title: On Some Open Problems of Mahmoudi and Renshaw

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a monoid S and a cyclic right S-act A that does not admit a (P)-cover, where a cyclic right S-act is an act generated by one element (equivalently of the form S/ρ for a right congruence ρ), and a (P)-cover means a cover by an S-act satisfying condition (P): whenever as = a't, there exist a'', u, v with a = a''u, a' = a''v, and us = vt?

evidence.quote: 1. Is there a monoid S and a cyclic S-act A which does not have a (P)-cover? (The open problem 1 in [9].)

Remark 2.4. Theorem 2.3 gives an answer to the open problem 1 in [9]: Is there a monoid S and a cyclic S-act A which does not have a (P)-cover? By Theorem 2.3 we only need to choose an arbitrary free monoid S and its arbitrary right congruence ρ satisfying |C([1]ρ)| > 1, then the cyclic right S-act S/ρ has no (P)-cover.

accepted.question_text: Are strongly flat covers of cyclic right S-acts unique? Here a strongly flat cover means a cover C → A in which C is a strongly flat right S-act; in the paper, strongly flat acts are recalled as acts satisfying the interpolation conditions (P) and (E).

evidence.quote: 2. Are strongly flat covers unique? (The open problem 5 in [9].)

Remark 2.14. Theorem 2.13 gives an answer to the open problem 5 in [9]: Are strongly flat covers unique? That is, there exist a monoid S and a right congruence on S such that the covers of cyclic right S-act S/ρ is not unique. More importantly, Theorem 2.11 and Theorem 2.13 show that there always exist a monoid and a cyclic act A such that A has as many strongly flat covers or (P)-covers as we want.

accepted.question_text: If S is an infinite inverse semigroup, must every cyclic right S-act S/ρ admit a (P)-cover? Here an inverse semigroup is a semigroup that is regular and whose idempotents commute, a cyclic right S-act is an act generated by one element, and a (P)-cover is a cover by an act satisfying condition (P).
accepted.context_brief: Cyclic acts over infinite inverse semigroups

evidence.quote: In [9] the author also posed the open problem: Do infinite inverse semigroups have the property that all cyclic S-acts have a (P)-cover? (The open problem 2 in [9].) In the following we will consider this problem.
Theorem 2.21. Let S be an infinite inverse monoid. If all left unitary submonoids of S are right unitary, then all cyclic S-acts have a (P)-cover.
